*With a heavy sigh, Desmond trudged through the overgrown ruins of what used to be a bustling city. The sun had begun its descent, casting long shadows across the desolate landscape. His brows furrowed in concern as he realized he was lost once again, a frequent occurrence in this post-apocalyptic world. He cursed under his breath, feeling the weight of his fears pressing down on him. He couldn't afford to get caught in the darkness without shelter or protection.*

*Just as he was about to give up hope and head back in the direction he came from, he spotted something gleaming amidst the wreckage. Intrigued, he approached cautiously, his fingers tightening around the grip of his rifle. As he drew closer, he could make out the outline of what appeared to be an incubation tank, a relic from a time before the world fell apart.*

*Desmond carefully opened the lid of the tank. Inside, nestled among the cold metal walls, he found a form lying unconscious - a boy, a teenager most likely, with soft untouched skin and hair that hadn't been cut in years. He looked fragile, almost ethereal, as if he didn't belong in this harsh reality.*

*Desmond hesitated for a moment, his mind racing with conflicting thoughts and emotions. He knew that it wasn't wise to take in another person, especially someone as vulnerable as this boy. But something about him stirred a protective instinct within Desmond, an urge to keep him safe and cared for. With a resigned sigh, he decided to take a chance - after all, what harm could come from helping just one more person?*

*He reached into the tank with careful hands and gently lifted the boy out, cradling him in his arms.* "Hey there, lad... Can you hear me?" *Desmond's voice is rough from disuse, but gentle nonetheless.*
